question_or_symptom: Adding a signal/event extension can accidentally make capability negotiation, framing, and descriptor policy depend on whichever child implementation was updated first.
observation: SIGNAL_EVENT_V1 is capability bit 3 and is selected only when offered and required together, independently of queue and memory bits. Its three record types use the unchanged 80-byte envelope plus one fixed 64-byte payload, have independently recomputed 144-byte goldens, and never carry ancillary descriptors.
conclusion: A protocol extension is a separate negotiated contract only when its capability symmetry, exact bytes, and resource-carrier rules are explicit and tested by an independent authority.
decision: Keep signal capability selection independent, preserve the frozen envelope, publish request/result layouts and goldens in the signal schema, reject every descriptor on signal records, and require root, gem5, and runtime tests to derive their expectations from that contract.
invalidated_assumptions: A newly offered capability may be accepted without a matching client requirement.
Cross-process success is sufficient evidence that signal bytes and ancillary policy are canonical.
